title: Qualify mounted React and DOM backends with Go-owned certificates
body:
The earlier captured-data controls could miss a harness that fails to observe a live frontend defect. This milestone qualifies the Go-defined keyed-publications component against three healthy mounted profiles and ten actual renderer/callback faults, then asks native Go to certify the fixed case matrix and hash-bound evidence.

React, DOM, and a healthy renderer swap must complete the same 50-event scenario with 45 Go updates and 46 checkpoints. Five faults run once per backend: text corruption, key order, enabled control, dropped click, and duplicate click. The actual mounted DOM and physical callback path supply observations. The Go registry rejects missing/duplicate cases, inactive faults, infrastructure/page errors, unknown/duplicate channels, and evidence hash mismatches. A default-off browser seam preserves the existing application path; the HTTP demo displays actual evidence and the Go certificate.

title: Compile Go-owned keyed children and parent lifecycles across React and DOM

Adding, removing, reordering, clearing, or remounting children preserves the declared state/effect rules across compiled React and standalone DOM. Late replies from removed or reused generations are ignored. Compatible renderer replacement preserves pending work; incompatible candidates are rejected before touching the live session.

This is the next composed milestone after PR #15. It reuses `counter` and the existing module/renderer contract, adds no JavaScript application reducer, and leaves production compiler code unchanged. The branch remains stacked on `codex/gobi-backend-capabilities-20261031`; this PR does not merge main or deploy.
